transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

The E18 error code on your Bosch washing machine (including the WAN28281GB model) specifically indicates a drainage problem. This means the machine has detected that it cannot drain the water from the drum within the expected time frame.

Since you mentioned there is still water in the drum, this confirms the issue: the pump is either blocked, faulty, or unable to push the water out.

### ✅ Immediate Steps to Fix It

Here’s a step-by-step guide to troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue yourself:

#### 1. Check for Obstructions in the Drain Pump Filter
This is the most common cause (approx. 80% of E18 errors).
• Locate the filter: It’s usually behind a small flap at the bottom right-hand corner of the machine front.
• Prepare for water spillage: Place towels or a shallow tray underneath, as water will drain out when you open it.
• Unscrew the filter slowly (counter-clockwise) to let water drip out first.
• Remove the filter and check for debris: coins, buttons, lint, hair, or small objects.
• Clean the filter thoroughly under running water. Also, reach inside the filter housing with a finger or torch to check for any blockages deeper in the pump impeller area.
• Reinsert the filter tightly (clockwise) and close the flap.

#### 2. Check the Drain Hose
• Ensure the drain hose at the back of the machine is not kinked, crushed, or bent sharply.
• Check that the end of the hose (where it connects to your household waste pipe or sink standpipe) is not clogged or inserted too far down the pipe, which can create a siphon effect or blockage.
• The hose should be between 60cm and 90cm from the floor. If it’s too high or too low, drainage can fail.

#### 3. Reset the Machine
• After cleaning the filter and checking the hose:
• Turn the machine off using the power button.
• Unplug it from the wall for 1–2 minutes.
• Plug it back in and start a new drain/spin program to see if the error clears.

#### 4. Check for Foreign Objects
• Look inside the drum for small items (coins, bra wires) that may have fallen behind the rubber door seal or into the pump.

---

### ⚠️ If the Problem Persists

If you’ve cleaned the filter and checked the hose but the E18 error remains:
• The drain pump motor may be faulty and need replacement.
• There could be a blockage further down your household drainage system (less common, but possible if multiple appliances share a waste line).
• The pressure switch or sensor may be malfunctioning (rare).

### 🛠️ When to Call a Professional
If you’re uncomfortable performing these steps, or if the error continues after cleaning the filter and resetting:
• Contact Bosch Customer Service or a qualified appliance repair technician.
• Mention the model number (WAN28281GB) and the E18 code.

> 💡 Tip: Always run a drain/spin cycle periodically if you wash items that shed lint (like towels) to prevent future blockages.

Let me know if you’d like help locating the filter or interpreting any other error codes!

Thanks, I'll start with the filter. I'll get a tray and towels ready first. Is there anything I should do about the water still in the drum before I unscrew it? There's about a third of a drum full and a hum from the front when it tries to drain. No burning smell.

That "hum" is actually very helpful diagnostic information. It tells us that the pump motor is receiving electricity and trying to work, but something is physically preventing it from spinning or moving water effectively. Since there's no burning smell, the motor itself likely isn't burnt out yet—it’s probably just jammed by debris or a blockage.

Here is how you should handle the water in the drum before you unscrew the filter:

### 1. How to Remove the Water Safely
You don’t have to remove all the water manually, but it will make cleaning much easier and less messy. Here are two ways to do it:

Option A: The "Sponge & Towel" Method (Easiest)
• Use a large sponge or several thick towels to soak up as much water as you can from the drum and the door seal area.
• This reduces the volume of water that will spill out when you open the filter.

Option B: The "Siphon" Method (If you have a hose)
• If you have a short piece of clear plastic tubing (like an aquarium air pump tube), you can siphon the water out into a bucket.
• One end goes in the drum, the other end goes into a lower bucket. Suck on the upper end briefly to start the flow, then quickly place that end in the bucket.

### 2. Important Safety Step: The Emergency Drain Hose
Many Bosch models (including your WAN28281GB) have an emergency drain hose hidden behind the kickplate at the bottom front of the machine.
• Look for a small black rubber tube with a cap, usually tucked to the side or under the flap where the filter is.
• If you can access this, you can remove the cap and let the water drain into a shallow tray or bucket. This empties most of the drum before you even touch the main filter.

### 3. When You Unscrew the Filter
When you finally unscrew the main pump filter:
• Open it slowly: Let the remaining water trickle out first before pulling the filter all the way out.
• Check the impeller: Once the filter is out, look inside the pump housing. You’ll see a small plastic wheel (impeller). Try spinning it with your finger. If it’s stuck or hard to turn, that confirms debris is jamming it. Clear any lint, hair, or objects around it.

### 4. After Cleaning
• Reinsert the filter tightly.
• Run a Drain/Spin program only (if available) or a short cotton cycle to test if the water drains properly and the error clears.

Let me know how you get on with the filter! If the impeller spins freely but it still won’t drain, we may need to look at the pump itself or the hose further down.
Thanks, I'll try the emergency drain hose first and then do the filter. I'll report back once I've done it.

That sounds like a solid plan. Using the emergency drain hose will make cleaning the filter much less messy since you won't have to deal with that third of a drum full all at once.

Just keep an eye on that "hum" while you're working—if the pump is jammed by debris, it might struggle even more once the water level drops, so be ready for some resistance when you check the impeller inside the filter housing.

Take your time and let me know how it goes!

Ok, I've done the emergency hose and the filter. It took several trays and towels to empty the water, and it was grey and smelled a bit. The filter had a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it, plus lots of fluff. The floor got a little wet while I was doing it. What should I check next?

That explains everything! A sock and a hair grip are exactly the kind of items that can jam the pump impeller or block the drainage path completely. It’s great you found them so quickly—those are common culprits for E18 errors.

Since you've cleared the filter, here is what to check next:

### 1. Check the Pump Impeller
With the filter removed, look into the hole where it was. You should see a small plastic wheel (the impeller).
• Try spinning it with your finger. It should turn freely and smoothly.
• If it feels stiff or stuck, there might be another piece of debris (like a coin or button) hidden deeper in the pump housing that the sock didn't catch.

### 2. Reassemble Carefully
• Make sure the filter is screwed back on very tightly. A loose filter can cause leaks and prevent the machine from building enough pressure to drain properly, which could trigger another error.
• Ensure the emergency drain hose cap is also closed securely.

### 3. Reset and Test
• Plug the machine back in and turn it on.
• Run a Drain or Spin program first (if your model has one) to see if it clears the remaining water without error.
• If that works, run a short cotton cycle at 40°C to ensure everything is functioning correctly.

### A Quick Note on the Smell
The grey water and smell are normal for a machine that hasn't been drained in a while or has had clothes sitting in stagnant water. Once you've cleared the blockage:
• Consider running an empty 90°C "Clean Drum" cycle with some washing machine cleaner or white vinegar to help remove any lingering odors from the pump and drum.

Let me know if the impeller spins freely or if the error comes back during that first test run!
I checked the impeller with the power off. It turned, a bit notchy at first and then free. I put everything back and ran a rinse and spin. It drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spun normally.

That is excellent news! 🎉 The fact that the impeller was "notchy" initially confirms that the sock and hair grip were indeed jamming the pump mechanism. Once you removed them, the water could flow freely again, which cleared the E18 error.

Since the machine is now working correctly, here are a few final tips to keep it running smoothly:

• Clean the Drum: Because there was stagnant grey water in the drum for a while, I'd recommend running an empty 90°C cycle with a washing machine cleaner or some white vinegar. This will help remove any lingering odors and clean out any residual fluff from the pump housing.
• Regular Filter Checks: Since you found significant debris this time, it's worth checking the filter every 3–4 months to prevent future blockages.
• Pocket Patrol: Always give clothes a quick pocket check before washing to catch items like hair grips and coins that can cause these issues later on.

You've done a great job troubleshooting this yourself! If you notice any other strange noises or error codes in the future, feel free to reach out. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your Bosch?
